title: Adaptive slack sampler with timebox gating for continuous batcher
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduce an adaptive slack sampler and timebox gating for the continuous batcher to reduce p99 latency in KV-heavy workloads. Backward compatible behind feature flag; rollout via canary. Improves p99 by ~12% in internal benchmarks with minimal throughput impact.
commits: feat(batcher): add adaptive slack sampler and timebox gating (initial impl)
perf(batcher): tune slack percentile and decay window; add metrics
chore(tests): add integration and perf harness scenarios for KV-heavy tails
fix(batcher): handle zero-occupancy edge case and avoid negative slack
docs: describe new sampler and rollout guidance in batcher.md
discussion_threads: Ethan Morris: This looks promising; main concern is the interaction between slack decay window and autoscaling. Can we prove it doesn't create oscillation?
Author (Asha Patel): Added a decay hysteresis and a max-step limiter; bench harness shows no oscillation across 0/20/100% KV mixes. See metrics added under batcher.sampler.*
Lina Zhou: Please add a guard for zero-slot hosts to avoid fractional slack -> negative gating; also ensure telemetry exposes cohort sizes.
Author (Asha Patel): Fixed zero-occupancy edge and added cohort_size and effective_slack metrics. Unit test included.
Owen Park: Approved after seeing integration results and canary rollout plan.
description: Context: We see persistent p99 tail latency in continuous-batcher when a small number of KV-heavy 'pin' requests occupy long-lived slots; existing deadline heuristics either favour throughput (allowing starvation) or favour fairness (reducing throughput). Motivation: reduce long-tail latency without large throughput regressions and provide an operationally-safe rollout path. What this PR does: 1) Introduces an adaptive slack sampler that computes a per-cohort 'slack' budget based on recent slot occupancy percentiles and request duration histograms, using an exponentially weighted percentile estimator. Slack is the additional time a request may linger in the active window before being considered for eviction or preemption. 2) Adds a timebox gating layer that enforces an upper bound on how long a request may be allowed to persist in the head of the continuous batcher queue; the timebox is dynamically adjusted by the sampler but clamped to safe min/max values. 3) Integrates prefetch hints into KV pipeline: requests that declare KV-prefetch intent can be sampled more conservatively to avoid mass prefetch churn. 4) Telemetry: new metrics batcher.sampler.effective_slack, batcher.sampler.percentile_estimate, batcher.timebox.duration_ms, and cohort_size; these are surfaced in existing dashboards and used for alerts. Design details: - Slack calculation: use the 90th/95th percentile of observed slot hold times with EWMA smoothing (configurable alpha) and apply a decay hysteresis to avoid rapid swings. - Timebox gating: when head request hold time > effective_slack, we start soft-preemption probes with jittered backoff; if a request exceeds timebox hard-limit, it is demoted to background queue for fairness. - Safety: feature-flagged behind batcher.feature.adaptive_slack in helm values; default off for clusters >= prod; enabled in canary envs. - Rollout: staged canary: 5 hosts (1%) -> 20 hosts (5%) -> 100 hosts (20%) -> full. Automated rollback if error_budget > 5% or p50 latency degrades by >5% and p99 does not improve. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for percentile estimator, slack decay hysteresis, and zero-occupancy guard. - Integration tests in integration/batcher/kv_tail_test.go simulating mixed KV/non-KV traffic. - Perf harness: synthetic KV tail workloads run on benchmark-lab with 3 seeds; results: p99 reduced by 12% (median across seeds), p95 reduced by 7%, overall throughput change -2% under heavy KV scenario. - Observability: new dashboard panels and alerts for effective_slack and cohort_size; added logs at debug level for sampling decisions. Files changed (high level): - pkg/batcher/continuous_sampler.go: new sampler implementation, including EWMA percentile estimator and config options. - pkg/batcher/timebox_gate.go: gating logic and demotion hooks. - runtime/scheduler/cohort.go: cohort metadata tracking and slot occupancy sampling. - runtime/kv/cache.go: prefetch hint plumbing and lightweight token to inform sampler. - pkg/telemetry/metrics.go: metrics registration and tags. - integration tests and docs. Review notes and iterations: - First CI run failed due to an edge-case where hosts with transient zero-occupancy produced negative slack; fixed by clamping and unit test added. - Ethan requested autoscaling oscillation tests; added decay hysteresis and bench to prove stability. - Lina requested extra telemetry for cohort sizes; added metric and dashboard snippet. Operational impact and rollback: - Backward compatible and disabled by default. Helm flag in helm/values/batcher-featureflags.yaml toggles the sampler. - Rollout includes canary gating and automated metric checks; rollback documented in docs/operational/batcher.md. Known limitations: - In extremely bursty workloads with very short sequences, the estimator needs longer windows to converge—this will be addressed in a follow-up that adds adaptive windowing. - Prefetch hinting requires callers to opt-in; without hints the sampler conservatively assumes worst-case. Merge: Squash-merged into main after approvals and successful canary. Summary: This PR provides a practical middle path between strict deadline enforcement and throughput-first behavior by adaptively computing slack and enforcing a timebox. Benchmarks show meaningful p99 improvements for KV-heavy tails with minimal throughput cost.
